#1947. Hammers favourite reveals Nuno’s part in his decision to quit West Ham

One of the major disappointments from this summer of change was seeing Hammers’ academy graduate Freddie Potts leave the club where he’d been since he was a seven year old. A ten million transfer fee justified the move in most fans’ minds, but there was still a sense of unfulfilled promise, despite Potts’ finally achieving his dream of a Premier League debut for the team he loved and had supported as a child.

In a candid interview today with BBC.co.uk, Potts reveals why he chose to quit West Ham United.

Without putting too fine a point on it, the whole move to Belgian Champions FC Brugge came about through manager Nuno Espirito Santo’s selection choices and Potts being sidelined, as he explained:

“In pre-season my minutes with West Ham were limited, they weren’t as much as I wanted and then I spoke with my agent and said ‘let’s explore options because this season I’m 22, turning 23’,” Potts said.

“It’s a massive part of my career and I wanted to play.”

Nuno’s decision to limit Potts’ game time led to his decision to quit the club

Subsequently the interest from Brugge- now competing in the Champions League against the likes of Liverpool this very week – arose and Potts grabbed at the chance:

“The opportunity of Club Brugge came along with Champions League football, the best club in Belgium and it was an opportunity I couldn’t really turn down with how my minutes were going down with West Ham.

“I grew up in the area, going to the stadium watching the games. It was always going to be a tough decision but it was something that I had to do for my career.”

And who can blame him: Freddie lines up against Liverpool this week in the Champions League – the same week in which his old club head for a second division mid table scrap with Portsmouth. Good decision young man. Go and win it.

#1945. GdS: Tough skin and Dzeko precedent – Ramos has time to reverse flop status

Goncalo Ramos has struggled to find the back of the net with the AC Milan shirt so far, with the Rossoneri hoping that he will eventually find his groove.

After years of struggling in the No.9 position, following the departure of Olivier Giroud, Gerry Cardinale said enough is enough and spent over €70m on Ramos this summer. However, at least so far, it seems that wasn’t the right solution after all.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Portuguese striker has only scored three goals for the Rossoneri so far, despite featuring in every single game except one. Meanwhile, Alphadjo Cisse has eight goals to his name and cost almost ten times less than the No.9.

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport, if we were to conduct a survey today, Ramos would be the undisputed leader of seasonal flops for many. The fact that Milan are even considering investing another €50m+ in another striker says a lot.

Of course, such a move shouldn’t be seen as the Rossoneri demonstrating their lack of confidence in the striker. On the contrary, since Cardinale wants to aim for the Scudetto, having two very strong strikers would only be natural.

Still, Ramos needs to step up his goalscoring either way. The hard work he puts in every game, while recognised by the fans, isn’t enough as the usual “that’s not what a striker should do” always follows that praise. The old cliché is true: for strikers, scoring goals is the most important thing.

As the pink newspaper continues, given their characteristics and quality on the ball, Edin Dzeko is a good precedent for Ramos to cling to. The Bosnian arrived in Rome from Manchester City and struggled a bit in his first season (eight league goals), causing a headache for everyone involved.

However, in the following season, he bagged a whopping 29 league goals with the help of Luciano Spalletti’s trust and the assists from Francesco Totti and Mohamed Salah. His resurgence was remarkable, so it’s something Ramos can take inspiration from.

#1944. Sabah vs Barcelona - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 13:30, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43

Barcelona will aim to make it five straight wins in all competitions when they continue their Champions League campaign away to Sabah on Wednesday night.

History will be made in this contest, as the two teams prepare to lock horns for the first time, and it would be one of the biggest shocks in Champions League history should Sabah manage to overcome the La Liga champions.

Sabah boast a record of one win and three draws from their four matches in this season's Champions League league phase, which has left them in 31st spot in the table on three points, one point behind 24th-placed PSV Eindhoven.

The Owls opened their league stage campaign with a 4-0 loss to Manchester United, before managing to record a 2-0 victory over Slavia Prague in their second fixture to put three points on the board, but they have since lost to Borussia Dortmund and Viking FC.

Valdas Dambrauskas's side will enter this match off the back of a huge domestic win, beating Sumqayit 5-1, with the result leaving them third in Azerbaijan's top flight, picking up 24 points from their opening 11 games of the season.

Including qualification matches, Sabah have a record of seven wins and five losses in this season's Champions League, keeping five clean sheets in the process.

The Owls had never played in the European Cup before this season, so it is a historic campaign for the club, and they will take on Villarreal, Napoli and Arsenal in their three Champions League league stage fixtures after this one.

As for Barcelona, the Catalan side are currently fifth in the league phase table, picking up nine points from their four matches courtesy of a record of three wins and one defeat.

Hansi Flick's side beat Feyenoord and Galatasaray in their opening two league stage fixtures before suffering a 4-2 reverse to Paris Saint-Germain, but they managed to post a 3-0 victory over Aston Villa last time out to get back on track.

Barcelona will enter this match off the back of a 3-2 win over Villarreal, with that result moving them back to the top of the La Liga table, three points ahead of Real Madrid.

The Catalan side lost in the last-16 stage of last season's Champions League to Atletico Madrid, and it remains to be seen whether their defensive unit is strong enough to make a serious challenge for the 2026-27 European Cup.

Barcelona have actually conceded in each of their last 12 away group stage/league phase matches, but they have scored at least twice in 17 of their last 19 games at this point.

Sabah will be without the services of Aden McCarthy, with the centre-back suspended on Wednesday following his red card in the team's last Champions League match with Viking.

The hosts also need to make a check on the fitness of Veljko Simic, who is struggling with an injury; the attacker has eight goals in 18 appearances this season and his absence would therefore be a major blow for Sabah.

Joy-Lance Mickels has been in impressive form this season, scoring 12 goals in 22 appearances, and the forward is set to start for the home team.

As for Barcelona, Lamine Yamal will not be involved due to a slight ankle problem, with Barcelona not prepared to take any risks when it comes to the Spain international.

Roony Bardghji (knee), Xavi Espart (ankle), Rodri (hamstring) and Andreas Christensen (muscle) are also unavailable for selection.

Pau Cubarsi did not play against Villarreal on Sunday due to an issue that he sustained while on international duty with Spain, but the centre-back was on the bench and should feature in the starting team.

Meanwhile, Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi are expected to join Raphinha in the final third of the field due to the absence of Yamal.

Pokatilov; Zedadka, Solvet, Almeida, Puchaz; Lepinjica, Isayev, Rakhomaliev; Severina, Mbina, Mickels

J Garcia; E Garcia, Cubarsi, Martin, Cancelo; Fermin, Bernal, Pedri; Adeyemi, Raphinha, Gordon

Yamal's absence is a major blow for Barcelona, but the Catalan outfit have enough quality in their side to secure all three points on Wednesday.

#1943. ‘Did you see any problems?’ – Hungary boss defiant over Dominik Szoboszlai decision

Hungary manager Marco Rossi has defended his usage of Dominik Szoboszlai during this international window.

The Liverpool midfielder sprained his knee during the Reds’ 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace the weekend before last and admitted that he nearly pulled out of his country’s win over Georgia six days later.

His choice to represent his nation was condemned by some reporters back on Merseyside, amid fears of aggravating the injury and compromising his involvement for his club over the coming weeks as the fixtures come thick and fast for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Rossi was defiant when quizzed about Szoboszlai ahead of Hungary’s match against Northern Ireland on Tuesday night.

He told reporters (via Origo Sport): “Did you see any problems with Dominik in the Georgia game? Because I didn’t see any. He played like he usually does, so there are no problems from our side. He says he’s ready, he’s available, so he’ll play.”

The Hungary boss was true to his word, as the Liverpool star played the entirety of the Northern Ireland game, thankfully seeming to come through it without any adverse effects.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

We can understand Szoboszlai wanting to represent his country, especially in his role as captain, but those who pay his wages at Anfield mightn’t have been overly impressed with his decision to play on despite knowing prior to the Georgia match that he wasn’t operating at 100%.

That Liverpool don’t play until Sunday at 4:30pm gives the 26-year-old that bit of additional time to manage his fitness carefully so that he’s in prime condition for the game against Manchester United.

Whether or not the midfielder will start that match is debatable. The in-form Alexis Mac Allister and Florian Wirtz will likely have two of the three midfield berths nailed down, and the excellent displays of Trey Nyoni have made it difficult to omit him from the XI.

Also, if Iraola feels that Szoboszlai isn’t fully fit by Sunday, he probably won’t take the risk of throwing our number 8 back into the starting line-up, instead keeping him in reserve should he be needed off the bench.

Hopefully the influential Hungarian won’t suffer any further complications over the next four days, and everyone associated with Liverpool will surely be glad that the international window is out of the way, with the next one not upon us until late March 2027.

#1942. West Ham will get back on track if they follow competitor example – report

The difference between success and failure in this division is measured in hundreds of millions of pounds. To the three promoted sides comes the financial mushroom cloud of Premier League cash – a veritable explosion to enable survival in the top tier – but to those who fail to climb out of the Championship – especially those with big budgets – comes financial obscurity and the very real risk of further budget slashing just to stay afloat.

Last season, Championship teams between them lost a worrying £300 million plus: An unsustainable model for football club survival and West Ham, with hugely diminished parachute payments, would face further swinging cuts to stay solvent. So promotion at the first attempt is crucial.

The Hammers would do well to take a leaf out of competitor Wolverhampton Wanderers’ books. Like West Ham, Wolves have stuttered without hitting top form and yet there they sit, third in the Championship. As footballleagueworld.co.uk report, they’ve ground out an impressive sequence of results:

“if Wolves haven’t always impressed with their performances, they have found a way of getting results, and they head into the Derby game unbeaten in seven, picking up 17 points in that period.”

“Wolves are just getting it done. Even when they haven’t been turning up (performances), they’ve been doing enough. So, it worries me that if they turn it on, and click into gear, and reach another level, they could be the ones.”

Winning ugly, they used to call it. And West Ham need to learn the lesson from their Black Country opponents and start grinding out results even if they are not playing fluid, attractive football.

Because it’s all about the points. And what do points make?

#1941. Bayern Munich stance on signing Real Madrid's Trent Alexander-Arnold 'revealed'

By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 13:32

Bayern Munich are reportedly not interested in signing Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold in the near future.

Alexander-Arnold established himself as arguably one of the finest right-backs in Premier League history during his time at Liverpool, but he has struggled to reproduce that form since joining Real Madrid.

The England international has gradually slipped down the pecking order at the Santiago Bernabeu under Jose Mourinho, with Federico Valverde and Denzel Dumfries seemingly ahead of him.

Alexander-Arnold was also subjected to boos from sections of the home support following his lacklustre performance in Real Madrid's 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo last week.

Former Liverpool and England striker Emile Heskey recently suggested that Alexander-Arnold should consider a move to Bayern, although he admitted he would love to see the defender return to Anfield.

However, Bild journalist Christian Falk has categorically dismissed the links, suggesting that Bayern are more interested in signing players such as Givairo Read than Alexander-Arnold.

Bayern already have Konrad Laimer and Josip Stanisic available for the right-back position, while Sacha Boey also remains at the club.

Even if Vincent Kompany decides to make changes in that department, he would reportedly favour a younger profile, meaning Alexander-Arnold is unlikely to be a genuine option for the German champions.

Speaking to CFBayern Insider, Falk said: "It is not true - Bayern Munich are interested in Real Madrid fullback Trent Alexander-Arnold. Bayern are searching for a player in this position, and players like Givairo Read are definitely still of interest.

"You can tell from Read’s profile alone that the club just isn’t looking to add a player like Alexander-Arnold to the ranks. Also, I’m not sure if Vincent Kompany would look at the Englishman’s profile, as he’s not a typical right-back for Bayern Munich.

"He’s also not the youngest footballer any more. And, if we’re being honest, the 28-year-old hasn’t proven himself at Real Madrid.

"You have to have a lot of respect for English players who give it a go playing in another country. But not every English player succeeds after leaving the UK, and not every English player is Harry Kane! So, I don’t think Alexander-Arnold will be a genuine option for Bayern in the summer."

While an emotional return to Anfield would appeal to many supporters, the reality is that Liverpool have probably moved on, even though the right-back position remains a somewhat problematic area for them.

Jeremie Frimpong has yet to convince everyone, while there is also uncertainty over whether the Reds will sign Ronald Araujo from Barcelona on a permanent deal.

With Conor Bradley's injury record remaining a concern and Joe Gomez potentially departing next summer, Andoni Iraola could look to bring in a new right-back, although it remains doubtful whether Liverpool would consider a move for their former player.

#1940. Amorim discusses ‘fun’ Frosinone, final third struggles and confirms Pavlovic’s return

On the eve of AC Milan’s game against Frosinone, Ruben Amorim spoke to the media at the usual pre-match press conference.

The international break is officially over and Milan will be back in action tomorrow. After wins against Inter and Genoa, the goal is to make it three consecutive wins, although an in-form Frosinone side will be looking to make life difficult for them.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Amorim’s plan appears to be to field an attacking-minded starting eleven, picking up where he left off against Genoa. It’s certainly a bold plan as Frosinone will surely look to cause issues on the counter, as also highlighted by Oliver in his prediction.

Speaking to the media at Milanello, Amorim shared his thoughts on the game, the status of the players after the international break, and the tactical solutions moving forward.

“We as a club have a big responsibility. Fondazione Milan is really important because it reflects our values and helps the community. Our doors are always open for everyone. It’s also good for the players to see and live different realities.”

“I think everyone is ready. Of course, we had to control the load during the week, because some of them travelled a lot. I’m really pleased with our players getting game time, because that’s the best way to maintain, so we are ready for the game.”

On Pavlovic’s status and Frosinone’s style..

“Starting with Pavlovic, he’s doing better. He will be in the squad. I don’t know if he will start or not, so I will see. He wants to play and I want him to play. We miss that fire that he has. Let’s see, but for sure he will be in the team.

“Frosinone are fun to watch, they are the team that runs the most, and we are second so I think we can fight that. They are really good with 1v1s on the flanks. If you watch their games it’s hard to understand their movement. There is some logic in their chaos, but it’s hard to spot.

“They play a different style, more direct, which allows them to have the ball more inside the box. So it’s going to be a really hard game. As I said against Venezia, there are some teams that we need to be really focused against because their styles can cause issues.”

Camarda is getting little game time, despite the Ramos struggles. Is a strong deputy striker missing?

“Two different questions. Of course we can say that one more option would be a good thing, but I think the struggles of Ramos are the struggles of the team. We are not reaching the final third, we are one of the worst teams in that sense. So we don’t have a lot of shots.

“I don’t want loads of shots outside the box, because it’s hard to score with those. We need to get into the box and we are not helping Ramos. What I saw against Genoa is that without Ramos, we wouldn’t have scored those goals. But again, we need to do better in the final third, my goal is to push the team forward. That’s my job.

“It’s true that he’s working hard and doing a lot of good. I know that it’s not his sole job to press, we spent a lot of money on a player to score goals, but we are not doing enough to help him. We need to push the team forward.”

Are you happy with the league standings so far? And against Genoa, you basically played with four attacking players. Can this be a solution for the future?

“Starting with the last question, it depends on the opponents and the moment of the team. I don’t believe that playing with more attackers means you will reach the final third more. Sometimes you get that effect from having more midfielders, for example. We are always going to change in some matches depending on the opponent.

“On the first question, it’s difficult to say. I think that we have grown as a team quite fast, but I’m not pleased with the overall situation. We need to be so much better and as such, I’m not pleased with where we are in the standings. But of course, I need to say that I’m happy with how the players have worked.”

During the break, we saw Camarda scoring for the U21s. Could a loan be the right solution?

“I was a young player myself once too. A young player wants everything really badly, which is a good thing. That said, he needs time to adapt, it’s really hard to play for a club like Milan. You just said there is pressure on Ramos, imagine what it’s like for Camarda.

“I don’t know what will happen in January, but he needs to be focused on these games. Everything can change in just a few weeks.

“I’m really happy with how he has been since he returned from international duty, I heard that Baldini spoke with him at length (as Baldini said himself), and he returned in a happier mood. I understand the question about January, but January is so far away right now.”

The feeling is that the team is struggling to keep control at the end of the games…

“Sometimes even when we are winning, we have dropped the levels in every action of the game. I think we are controlling everything better, you saw it in the second half against Genoa without spending a lot of energy, but I think it’s all connected to the attack.

“If we don’t create danger when we are leading, we will struggle a bit to kill the games. Of course, we need to address that and we are working on it.”

On Musah as a left-back and if more versatile players will be signed…

“That was a specific situation. I don’t know and I’m not going to tell you guys what we are thinking about January. I wanted a right-footed player against Genoa. You saw the runs of Rabiot, so I wanted someone right-footed to pass the ball on immediately.

“Musah is not going to play as a left-back tomorrow, I can tell you that, but it’s an option. I like to have players who can play in several positions.”

“I think it helps any player to feel the confidence from the club. I think it’s clear that was done with the new contract. Then I also told you when he wasn’t playing that he’s really important for us. I can tell you today that Pulisic perhaps is the one player we cannot replace.

“The movement in between the lines he brings, we simply don’t have another Pulisic. His absence is always felt a lot, so from that you can understand how important he is for us. He doesn’t talk a lot, but he lets the pitch do the talking.

“I would put him in the same category as Rabiot. Players who are on another level. I don’t like speaking about individuals, but I think everyone can see this.”

Can the January transfer window serve to raise the team’s ambition?

“That is the biggest mistake of the big clubs. Looking at the table and deciding whether to invest or not. I think the key is to have a long-term plan. Stick with your plan. We have one and everything is very clear.

#1939. New manager bounce? How Mauricio Pochettino fared in his first match in charge of previous clubs

Liverpool will be wary of the threat of ‘new manager bounce’ on Sunday when they face a Manchester United team now under the management of Mauricio Pochettino.

Having sacked Michael Carrick last Thursday, the Red Devils moved swiftly to appoint the Argentine as his successor, with their new head coach signing off from a similar role with the United States with a 2-0 win over Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League.

The Old Trafford outfit enjoyed an immediate upsurge in form when their former midfielder replaced Ruben Amorim back in January, but how has the new man in charge fared in his first game at his five previous spells as a club boss?

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Espanyol were in the LaLiga relegation zone when Pochettino took charge almost 18 years ago, and his first task seemed a daunting one against city rivals Barcelona, who’d end the season as treble winners under Pep Guardiola.

The Argentine had only two training sessions to implement his methods before the Copa Del Rey derby fixture, but his new team claimed an impressive share of the spoils on home turf before narrowly losing the second leg 3-2 at Camp Nou. A few weeks later, he masterminded a shock league victory at the home of their arch-rivals.

The Saints’ decision to axe the popular Nigel Adkins mid-season was met with shock throughout English football, with the south coast club well on their way to staying up in their first season back in the Premier League after a seven-year absence.

He again drew 0-0 in his first game of a managerial spell, with Southampton putting in a battling performance against an Everton side who, at the time, were outside contenders for Champions League qualification under David Moyes.

This was Pochettino’s first time having a full summer to prepare for a managerial job rather than coming in mid-season, earning the Spurs gig off the back of his fine work at Southampton.

The north Londoners survived a red card and a missed Mark Noble penalty before snatching all three points in stoppage time courtesy of an Eric Dier goal on what was also his first outing with Tottenham, who left the Boleyn Ground with a sweet win over their capital rivals.

It was back to mid-season appointments for Pochettino six-and-a-half years later as he filled the vacancy left by Thomas Tuchel’s departure for Chelsea.

He maintained his record of never losing his first game in charge of a club, but in truth this was two points dropped for PSG, who at the time were three points adrift of surprise Ligue 1 leaders Lyon. They also had to come from behind against an in-form Les Verts side.

Sunday won’t be the first time that Liverpool provide the opposition for Pochettino in his first game in charge – the Reds also had that role when the Argentine began his reign as Chelsea boss three years ago.

Once again he’d end with a draw, as an entertaining clash on the opening weekend of the Premier League season saw Luis Diaz’s opener for the visitors cancelled out by Axel Disasi as each team had a further goal disallowed.

Four draws and a win for Pochettino from his managerial debuts at his previous clubs – it’s a respectable record, but not an overly intimidating one.

It feels more pertinent to look at his first results when taking charge mid-season, just as he’s doing now with Man United. All three of those games were drawn, and another such result on Sunday would be regarded as a decent start for him.

It’d also represent disappointment for Liverpool, who are without an Anfield win over their arch-rivals in three attempts since the famous 7-0 romp in March 2023.

#1936. Report – West Ham prepared to cut their losses on January exit that suits all parties

From the sound of it, West Ham United are going all-in to refresh their options in front of goal in January. The club face a crisis with none of their trio of goal scorers looking fit for purpose: The best of the three, Joel Piroe, has amassed four goals this season whilst the other two have managed just one goal apiece.

Neither Pablo Felipe nor Taty Castellanos have fulfilled the expectations that were present when they were signed in the January window at the start of this year – Taty especially was expected to boss the Championship after the Hammers were relegated but at times he’s appeared no more than a scowling misfit, unable to influence games when he’s been called upon.

‘What a waste of money” as the song goes…

Footballinsider.com – who are usually on the ball with their reporting – have it apparently on good authority that West Ham are prepared to sanction his departure in January even though the club will have to absorb yet another huge financial hit:

“Sources: West Ham to accept Taty Castellanos loss ahead of January”

Runs their article, detailing West Ham’s willingness to sell the forward, despite being fully aware that they’ll not see anything like the £26 million they paid for the Argentine striker just twelve months ago:

“The 28-year-old has scored just one goal from 15 games in the Championship this season, and is performing way below the level West Ham expected from him.

Sources say that the East London outfit are prepared to sell Castellanos at a loss this winter, knowing that it will be “very difficult” to recoup the £26million they paid for him.”

This is the key: Taty had previously been linked with loan moves back to Argentina which were never really feasible. The fact that West Ham are apparently putting it ‘out there’ that they’ll take the hit in order to move the striker on means that bids should be forthcoming in the winter market from a number of clubs; several who’ll no doubt chance their arm hoping to get him for a bit of a steal.

One goal in 15 games in the second division is nothing to write home about though, and so West Ham’s approach is borne largely out of facing the undeniable fact that Castellanos has been a massive disappointment, not to mention a colossal waste of money.

#1934. Liverpool transfer news: New Alexis Mac Allister contract timeline given as two-year claim made (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 13:45

Liverpool are unlikely to give any consideration to a new contract for Alexis Mac Allister before February, Reds Champions League winner Didi Hamann has exclusively told Sports Mole.

The Argentina international is in the last two years of his current contract with Liverpool, having not signed a single extension since joining from Brighton & Hove Albion in the summer of 2023.

Mac Allister revealed in September that Liverpool were not in a position to offer him a new contract, after the 27-year-old experienced a noticeable decline in individual performance levels in 2025-26.

However, after a positive World Cup with Argentina, Mac Allister has returned to form for Liverpool, scoring five goals and providing one assist in 17 appearances across all competitions so far this season.

The midfielder has started nine of Liverpool's 11 Premier League games under Andoni Iraola and also performed well in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United, creating two chances, completing 89% of his passes and winning four of his five ground duels.

Nevertheless, ex-Liverpool midfielder Hamann does not believe that talks over a new deal will begin for another three months, and any extension is only likely to be two years at best.

"They said to him there's no contract now, and he's in his late 20s," Hamann told Sports Mole when asked if Mac Allister had already played his way into a new contract.

"If he carries on performing, if he keeps on scoring goals, then come February, March, April, there might be a time where you say. 'maybe we keep him another two years.' But I don't think there's any rush at the moment."

Mac Allister - who turns 28 on December 24 - has come up with 24 goals and 21 assists in 167 matches for Liverpool since 2023, and he earns £180,000 a week under his current contract terms, according to Capology.

The Argentine's reported salary only makes him the 11th highest-paid player at Liverpool, below new signing Ronald Araujo (£210k) and almost half of what Virgil van Dijk earns (£350k).

Mac Allister's relationship with Ryan Gravenberch blossomed to the maximum in the 2024-25 season, culminating in both midfielders becoming Premier League champions for the first time.

However, Mac Allister's decline from a defensive and box-to-box standpoint was striking; compared to 2024-25, he made 45% fewer tackles and 26% fewer recoveries than in the 2025-26 campaign.

Gravenberch's own form did not help the South American's cause, though, and the latter has had a rejuvenated look about him since the World Cup, immediately earning Iraola's trust in the process.

Mac Allister's availability remains exceptional too, as he has only missed 11 matches for club and country since joining Liverpool and has been involved in every match so far this season.

With Wataru Endo almost certainly on the way out and James McConnell still on the fringes, Liverpool should speed up the process of tying down Mac Allister, lest they risk losing another midfield option in 2027.

Didi Hamann was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of Lottoland Live Casino.

#1931. Liverpool must make January signing after telling Trey Nyoni comments

Trey Nyoni has admitted he ‘enjoys’ playing in the six position, but that it’s still a ‘new position’ for him.

The young Englishman has caught the eye with his performances at L4 this term, earning three straight starts across clashes with Arsenal (Premier League), Chelsea (Carabao Cup) and Fenerbahce (Champions League).

However, the teenager’s admission ultimately raises concerns around the midfield department ahead of the January transfer window.

It’s reassuring that links to Lamine Camara (who came close to a switch to Chelsea in the summer) have resurfaced ahead of the winter, given ongoing concerns over how Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch fit in an Andoni Iraola side.

While the performances of Alexis Mac Allister and Nyoni have undoubtedly mitigated matters, the truth of the matter is that Liverpool can’t look to rely on the latter of the duo throughout an entire campaign.

The Reds must, and no doubt will, look after the teenager to ensure his excellent development carries on smoothly, but his recent comments are a clear reminder that investment midway through the campaign is a necessity.

“I’ve been playing like a number six. I played there when I was young but, to be honest, it’s a new position for me. I’ve had to learn a lot in a short space of time,” Nyoni told The Inside Scoop (via BBC Sport).

“I enjoy playing like a six because I can get on the ball and always try to play forwards, but I enjoy playing as an eight as well.

“I like to drop in, get the ball and play forward but I’ve had to learn the discipline of being a number six.

“Right now, I don’t really have a preference. As I’m starting out, I enjoy playing both.”

We have faith that Iraola’s demands will eventually click with Gravenberch and Szoboszlai, but it’s still painful to see how open Liverpool look in the middle of the park when Mac Allister is forced to share space with either of his senior midfield partners. And the less said about a double pivot consisting of the Dutchman and the Hungarian, the better.

Yes, it’s fair to point out that our season is far from spiralling under Iraola — the Reds sit fourth in the Premier League table with only four points standing between them and Fabian Hurzeler’s high-flying Brighton in second.

But it does feel like there is an opportunity for Liverpool to make a modest statement in 2026/27. Not quite title glory, it has to be said, but certainly to stake a claim as “best of the rest” and set a promising foundation for the seasons to come under Iraola.

Adding an additional midfielder (like, cough cough, Lamine Camara, cough cough) to the ranks who can carry out the Basque’s demands would undoubtedly serve that purpose.

Elsewhere, the backline looks in fine shape and the forward line evidently needs time to gel. Give the manager the tools he needs in midfield and this could be an impressive opening campaign for Andoni Iraola.

#1930. Portsmouth 1 – 0 West Ham United | The morning after

West Ham’s manager Scott Parker, from his demeanour last night, is understandably in a pretty dark place just now after losing his second game in charge, four games now without a win: West Ham now twelfth in the second division with two points from their last eighteen.

“If you are going through hell, keep going” is the oft-quoted popular saying, accredited to Winston Churchill but applicable to just about any circumstance when deep in the smelly stuff.

It’s only football. We understand. But it is supposed to be the very salvation from all of the bad things going on in the world right now.

Which is why it feels pretty lousy being a West Ham fan right now, especially those intrepid away fans who braved the worst of the British transport system and weather to turn up and support their team at Fratton Park.

“The day is darkest just before the dawn” – It was pretty damn’ dark at Fratton Park last night

Most worrying of all is that the Championship’s top scorers seemingly now cannot put the ball in the back of the net.

However, a sneaky peek at the ‘bookies latest odds suggest they know something we don’t, with West Ham still odds-on (3/10 this morning) to finish in the top six. #1929. Man Utd make decision on what to do next after Leny Yoro's controversial red card against Liverpool

By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 13:57, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 14:51

Manchester United have reportedly notified the FA of their intention to appeal Leny Yoro's red card.

The centre-back was sent off during Man Utd's 4-0 defeat against Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League on Sunday after bringing down Alexander Isak as the striker raced through on goal.

The Red Devils were reduced to 10 men just eight minutes into the contest, a moment that significantly altered the complexion of the game as Liverpool enjoyed greater possession and created better opportunities.

While Man Utd could arguably have done more to frustrate the Reds, there is little doubt that Yoro's dismissal had a major bearing on the outcome.

According to Sky Sports, the Red Devils intend to appeal Yoro's dismissal, with Mauricio Pochettino offering his interpretation of the incident after the game.

The main point of contention is whether the foul constituted a clear denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity, with questions surrounding whether Isak was actually in control of the ball.

Under the laws of the game, one of the considerations when determining whether a player should be sent off for Denying an Obvious Goal-Scoring Opportunity (DOGSO) is whether the attacking player had control of the ball.

Pochettino not only questioned that aspect of the decision but also highlighted the referee's failure to penalise Jeremy Jacquet for his challenge on Bryan Mbeumo at the opposite end just moments earlier.

It remains to be seen how the FA will assess the incidents, although former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher has backed the on-field decisions in both cases.

Unless the decision is overturned following an appeal, Yoro is set to serve a one-match domestic suspension rather than a three-match ban, as his denial of a obvious goalscoring opportunity was a non-violent offence.

While the defender is available to face Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday, he will miss Man United's next Premier League fixture at home to Brentford on Saturday.

Yoro will then be available to return to Premier League action on December 2 when Pochettino's side travel to St James' Park to take on Newcastle United.

The Red Devils are now without a win in their last nine Premier League matches and have slipped to 19th in the table, with only Crystal Palace faring worse.

#1926. Man City charges: Jeremy Doku's response to “juicy” discussion on guilty Premier League verdict

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 13:59

Jeremy Doku was the latest Manchester City player to be questioned on his thoughts regarding the club’s Premier League financial charges case during a press conference on Monday.

An independent commission has found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the investigation.

In a verdict delivered at the end of September, the Citizens are accused of using "sham" contracts with a number of commercial partners to disguise secret funding of more than £830m and artificially inflate revenues between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 campaigns.

Man City have repeatedly expressed their innocence and lodged an appeal last month, stating that “a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.”

Should Man City’s guilty verdict be upheld, the club would be in danger of a plethora of possible sanctions, including heavy fines, transfer bans, stripping titles, points deductions leading to relegation and expulsion from the Premier League.

On the pitch, Man City have recently suffered a dip in form, failing to win any of their last four Premier League games (D1 L3), but manager Enzo Maresca played down suggestions that the 115 charges case is distracting his players - something Didi Hamann disagrees with.

Since September’s verdict, the likes of captain Ruben Dias and star striker Erling Haaland have faced questions on the ongoing legal case, and Doku is now the latest City star to be asked for his views on the matter.

However, Doku politely declined to comment on the club’s situation and was keen to discuss on-field matters only when speaking to the media ahead of City’s Champions League clash with Napoli on Tuesday.

“I know this is all juicy for you guys, but we have a big week; Napoli tomorrow, and then Arsenal," the Belgium international told reporters on Monday.

"So I think there's enough to speak about there instead of speaking about the charges. I'm not the person to speak about the charges, so with all respect I don't really want to be on that topic. We can speak about football, that's no problem."

In August, just a month before the guilty verdict was published, Doku extended his contract with Man City until the summer of 2031, and the winger has no regrets over his decision.

"I signed because I was happy to sign. I didn't think about anything else,” Doku clearly stated after being asked whether the charges came into his conversations over a new contract.

"I don't think it was a difficult thing for me. When you look at this club, how big of a club it is, the trophies they won and everything, it was an easy choice for me.

"I was happy here, I am happy here, I have a wife here, a son, it was an easy choice for me. So I didn't think a lot, obviously everything needed to be right for me to sign, but as soon as everything was right on both sides, it was an easy choice for me."

Assessing Man City’s season so far from an individual and collective perspective, Doku added: "I think I can do better. I started off with an injury this season, then came back well.

“And then the team, we did well with the first seven [Premier League] games where we won, and afterwards it was a bit more tough. As everyone knows, at the moment it's a bit more difficult, but I'm sure we'll bounce back, me as well."

Doku is a strong contender to start for Man City in their Champions League clash against Napoli, with the Citizens seeking to move one step closer to automatic last-16 qualification having already won three of their first four League Phase matches.

Maresca, meanwhile, has provided a positive update on the fitness of right-back Matheus Nunes, who missed the 1-1 Premier League draw with Fulham last weekend.

#1924. Galatasaray vs. Aston Villa: Unai Emery claims unusual Champions League preparation 'will not be an excuse'

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 14:03

Unai Emery has played down the significance of Aston Villa's unusual preparations for Tuesday's Champions League fixture at Galatasaray.

Having put together a five-game winless streak, Emery is coming under more scrutiny than he usually receives at Villa Park.

Victory at Rams Park would effectively guarantee Villa a place in the top 24 of the League Phase table and a spot in the knockout stages.

However, Villa have been required to change from the standard routine for a Champions League away game due to the condition of Galatasaray's pitch.

Although the match is not at risk of being postponed, UEFA has informed Villa that they cannot train at RAMS Park before the game, and the Premier League club opted against taking up the option of training at a different Turkish location.

Instead, Villa conducted their final training session at their own training facilities, while Emery held his pre-match press conference in Birmingham rather than Istanbul.

The Spaniard insisted that the amended schedule cannot be used as "an excuse" if Villa do not earn a result versus the Super Lig champions.

He told reporters: "It's not changing our usual way. We prefer to train here at Bodymoor and then travel to the country.

"We are doing some exceptions when we are playing a long way with a time change, we are training in the country - we did it last year at Fenerbahce.

"Of course if we could train at the stadium maybe we would decide to, but it's not changing our routine.

"It's not an excuse because it's for both teams. We are ready and we are focused and analysing the opponent."

Not only do Villa face Galatasaray this week, they make the trip to play Ipswich Town on Saturday evening in a key Premier League match.

Villa remain with just three wins from 11 matches in England's top flight, and failure to prevail against either Galatasaray or Ipswich would leave Emery going seven matches without a win when he is due to sign a new contract.

While Emery has total backing from the club's hierarchy and supporters, it is clear he needs to end their current run of form as soon as possible.

#1921. GdS: Possession vs. directness – key tactical differences between Milan and Frosinone

Ruben Amorim will be up against Massimiliano Alvini tomorrow evening, and as the stats show, they are two very different managers.

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport, there is one interesting stat to highlight to introduce the game. In terms of shots per game, it will be the second-ranked team and against the 17th-ranked team. That in itself won’t raise any eyebrows, but the fact that Milan are the ones in 17th place will.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri have mustered a mere 126 shots so far, while Frosinone are quite far ahead at 221. On the flip side, the newly-promoted side have only scored one more goal than Milan (24 vs. 23), which is what makes this game so interesting.

Amorim has made it clear from the start that he wants to dominate each game. That shows in the possession, as Milan are third in Serie A with an average of 59% so far, and they also rank high in terms of passes per game.

The shots are where they fall short, even if they average over two goals per game. There are several reasons for this, but most of it can be attributed to Amorim’s recent arrival and the fact that he has experimented rather extensively.

During today’s presser, he even said that they haven’t done anywhere near enough to enter the penalty box more often, which tends to mean more shots.

In the build-up, for example, the Rossoneri move the ball forward at an average speed of 1.30 meters per second, which is the slowest in Serie A. Alvini’s Frosinone, on the other hand, are great at vertical football: the ball moves toward the opponent’s penalty box at 2.51 meters per second, the best rate in the league.

The Ciociari are masters of rapid counterattacks, so much so that on only 40 occasions have they built plays with ten or more passes. Milan, meanwhile, have 203.

Everything starts in the defence phase for Frosinone. Indeed, they always attempt to win the ball back inside the opponent’s half, which is proven by the index that measures the intensity of pressing in the attacking zone (they are first in Serie A)

Milan? They are eighth, despite being – along with Como – the team to have scored the most goals (4) from a ball recovered while pressing.

The difference between the two is well explained by the so-called “pressed sequences”, that is, the number of actions in open play in which a team manages to interrupt the opponent’s build-up within three passes or less, before the ball goes beyond the halfway line.

On that front, Frosinone are also first (161), while Milan are only 15th (102). Having said all of this, as the pink newspaper concludes, we should expect a spectacular match tomorrow. Both teams will stick to their respective game, which bodes well.

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 14:45, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 15:11

Mauricio Pochettino could be without as many as seven Manchester United players for Wednesday’s Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon at the Estadio Jose Alvalade.

Former Sporting midfielder Manuel Ugarte (knee), Carlos Baleba (hamstring) and Benjamin Sesko (calf) all remain sidelined with injuries, while Luke Shaw (muscle), Marcus Rashford (hip) and Karl Darlow (knee) are all doubtful and will need assessing ahead of kickoff.

Matheus Cunha scored two late goals in Man United’s 3-2 comeback victory over Roma on matchday four, but he was then sent off for two bookable offences and will now serve a one-match suspension on Wednesday.

Leny Yoro, meanwhile, is available to return to the UCL squad after serving his own one-game ban following a red card against Atletico Madrid last month – he also received a straight red card in Man United’s heavy 4-0 Premier League defeat to Liverpool on Sunday, but will instead serve a domestic ban for that dismissal.

Yoro could therefore continue as a centre-back against Sporting, with Pochettino to weigh up whether to stick with a back three/five system with wing-backs or revert to a four-man defence.

Matthijs de Ligt was handed his first PL start in 357 games by Pochettino after recovering from a long-term injury, but the Dutchman endured a difficult return to the Red Devils side and may be pulled out of the starting lineup in midweek.

Harry Maguire would be the most likely name to replace De Ligt and could start as one of three central defenders next to Yoro and Lisandro Martinez, with Diogo Dalot and Patrick Dorgu operating as wing-backs.

Noussair Mazraoui is an alternative who could start as a right or left-sided full-back in a back four, or as a wing-back, with Dalot potentially operating on the opposite side, allowing Dorgu to push further forward and play in an attacking role.

Kobbie Mainoo, Youri Tielemans and captain Bruno Fernandes are expected to continue in their central midfield roles, the latter is set to face his former club for the first time since leaving to join Man United in January 2020.

Bryan Mbeumo could retain his starting spot as a centre-forward, but Pochettino may be tempted to hand Joshua Zirkzee a rare start up front, with Mbeumo moving over to the right side of attack. However, Amad Diallo could instead play on the right which would likely keep Mbeumo through the middle.

Manchester United possible starting lineup:

Lammens; Yoro, Maguire, Martinez; Dalot, Mainoo, Tielemans, Dorgu; Mbeumo, Fernandes; Zirkzee

#1919. Liverpool sending scouts ‘every week’ to watch red-hot sensation in shock Golden Boot contention

According to reports from Italy, Liverpool are regularly scouting a red-hot striker who’s emerged as a shock candidate for the Golden Boot in Serie A this season.

Andoni Iraola has been almost exclusively reliant on Alexander Isak at centre-forward since taking charge of the Reds in the summer, with Hugo Ekitike continuing his recovery from a long-term Achilles injury.

The Frenchman is targeting a return to action next month (The Athletic), although it appears that Anfield chiefs are keeping tabs on a positional alternative who’s emerging as a breakthrough sensation in one of Europe’s major leagues.

A report from Corriere dello Sport has claimed that Liverpool are sending scouts ‘every week’ to watch Gustavo Varela, who’s been in remarkable goalscoring form with Monza since joining the Serie A outfit in the summer.

Napoli and Juventus have also been strongly linked with the 21-year-old, who’s been the subject of enquiries from Tottenham, Brentford and Sunderland, with the list of suitors growing in tandem with his goal return in the Italian top flight.

Ivan Juric’s side reportedly want €40m (£33.5m) for the Portuguese hitman, which’d represent a monumental profit on a player they signed from Gil Vicente in July for a paltry €2.5m (£2.1m).

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Varela is currently the leading scorer in Serie A this season with nine goals, which is remarkable when his team are currently in the relegation zone, and he accounts for more than half of their goal tally in the top flight so far.

For someone who’d scored just seven times in 34 senior appearances before the summer, his form since joining Monza has been extraordinary. Should that continue, it’s safe to say that he won’t be at the Stadio Brianteo for much longer.

What Liverpool would need to consider is whether this is a mere purple patch from the Portuguese youngster, or the start of a journey towards being one of Europe’s most feared centre-forwards.

Varela has scored nine Serie A goals from an xG of just 5.48 (Fotmob), an astonishing overperformance which begs the question as to whether he can maintain that for a full campaign.

If Isak keeps up his own hot streak and Ekitike gets back to the levels he’d shown prior to his injury, it’d be difficult to see the Monza striker getting much of a look-in at Anfield.

However, it’s easy to see why Liverpool are routinely dispatching scouts to gather information on one of the breakout stars of European football in 2026.

#1917. ‘One source told me…’ – Liverpool journalist shares what he’s heard about Van Dijk ‘talks’

The future of Virgil van Dijk continues to be a much-discussed talking point going into the winter months.

The legendary Liverpool captain will see his current contract expire next June as things stand, with the Dutchman on track to become a free agent just before his 36th birthday.

Transfer insider Graeme Bailey recently claimed that there’s a strong chance of the veteran defender being offered at least a 12-month extension at Anfield, with Andoni Iraola unsurprisingly keen to keep hold of his skipper.

In his latest Liverpool Confidential feature for the Daily Mail, Lewis Steele reported of fervent interest from Serie A in Van Dijk amid ongoing speculation over the centre-back’s future.

The journalist wrote: ‘One source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides.

‘Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and influential adviser Zlatan Ibrahimovic are said to be huge admirers of Van Dijk, who turns 36 next summer.’

While the Rossoneri appear determined to pounce on any uncertainty over Van Dijk’s future, Steele added that the 35-year-old is ‘keen’ to extend his contract at Liverpool.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Any reports of interest in the Dutchman from other clubs will naturally trigger a level of concern among Reds supporters, but it’s natural that there’d be a queue of suitors for one of the best defenders of his (perhaps any) generation when he’s seven months away from becoming a free agent.

Until such time that a final decision is communicated by LFC, fans’ nerves will be frayed as to Van Dijk’s future. When we’ve already seen Mo Salah and Andy Robertson depart this year, the loss of another modern-day great in 2027 would represent a further gut punch for Kopites.

However, it’s worth remembering that when the Liverpool captain last penned a new contract in April 2025, he was just over two months away from leaving on a free, so he won’t panic even if there might be considerable gnashing of teeth outside of those involved in negotiations over his future.

James Pearce recently advised Reds supporters not to expect a ‘quick resolution’ over the defender’s situation, so for now, it seems that the best way for Van Dijk to secure a new deal at Anfield is to maintain the strong performance levels he’s shown so far this season.

The noise over his future is sure to continue for the time being, but we remain confident that everything will come together in due course and that our iconic number 4 will continue to grace the famous red shirt in the 2027/28 campaign.

#1916. Rangers vs Aberdeen - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 15:29, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 15:34

Rangers play host to Aberdeen on Tuesday night looking to move to within one point of leaders Celtic in the Scottish Premiership table.

Meanwhile, Aberdeen make the trip to Ibrox knowing that they could move into the top six with a surprise win over the Glasgow giants.

Although missing out on European football came as a major blow to Rangers at the time, it has enabled Derek McInnes's side to build up a head of steam on the domestic front.

Rangers have put together a 13-match unbeaten streak since that exit to Jablonec in the Conference League playoff round, recording 11 wins and two draws.

While being held to a 2-2 draw at Hearts before the November international break frustrated McInnes, Rangers have responded with a victory over Aberdeen in the League Cup and successive top-flight triumphs.

A 2-0 success at St Mirren was followed by an hard-earned 2-1 win at Motherwell on Saturday, Rangers sealing the three points through an 88th-minute own goal.

Eight of Rangers' 13 league matches have been played away from Ibrox, giving them a chance to make the most of competing on home territory, with seven goals being scored in their last two such games in the Scottish Premiership.

Over the international break, Liechtenstein legend Mario Frick was named as the new Aberdeen head coach.

The surprise development was followed by Frick delivering a 4-2 victory at Kilmarnock in his first game in charge.

A much-needed win has led to the Dons moving into eighth spot, albeit still just three points above the relegation zone.

With Aberdeen having lost five of the six matches preceding his arrival, Frick will not be getting carried away with three points versus bottom-of-the-table opposition.

Nevertheless, Aberdeen have now accumulated seven points from their most recent four away games in the Scottish Premiership, something which cannot be ignored by their hosts.

If McInnes makes any changes to his Rangers XI, Findlay Curtis and Kevin Kelsy are favourites to be introduced in the final third.

While Cameron Devlin is making progress in his recovery from injury, this game is expected to come too soon for the midfielder. The same applies to Lawrence Shankland, who has recently returned to light training after a significant hamstring injury.

Ryan Naderi has contributed either a goal or assist in eight of his last nine Scottish Premiership appearances.

Afeez Aremu, Findlay Marshall and Ayoub Mouloua are all options to return for Aberdeen after they made an impact from the substitutes' bench at Kilmarnock.

Connor Ronan remains an injury doubt after missing that fixture, while this match comes too soon for defender Mats Knoester. Chris Cadden is pushing for a return to the squad after a hamstring issue.

Pandur; Sterling, Makhanya, Fernandez, Rommens; Neil, Raskin; Bouanani, Naderi, Findlay; Kelsy

Muller; Devlin, Milne, Molloy, Guinness-Walker; Lyons, Aremu, Briedl; Marshall; Mouloua, Nisbet

With Aberdeen having made a positive start to life under Frick, they will back themselves to earn a result at Ibrox. However, given the chance to move within a point of Celtic, we feel that Rangers will do just enough to secure three points in a competitive fixture.

#1915. AC Milan Women 3-2 Sassuolo: Grimshaw crucial after crazy first half

Christy Grimshaw was crucial as AC Milan Women finally got back to winning ways, following what was a rather crazy first half against Sassuolo.

After two defeats and a draw, dropping points in a silly fashion against Napoli last weekend, Milan Women needed to bounce back with a win today. Thankfully, that’s exactly what they managed to do, even if it wasn’t the most controlled performance.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Just looking at the scoreline and the timing of the goals is enough to understand the nature of the game. All five goals were scored in the first half and it doesn’t end there either. All five were scored within the first 27 minutes!

The veteran Grimshaw opened the scoring for the Rossonere after nine minutes, but Sassuolo found a way back into the game just two minutes later. The Scottish international decided to restore the lead just four minutes later, i.e. in the 15th minute.

Angelica Soffia then made things more comfortable with a third goal in the 24th minute, or at least so we thought. Just three minutes after that, Sassuolo scored again and thus brought some life into the game, even if Milan looked the better side.

Suzanne Bakker’s side actually dominated possession, had more shots on target and also had a higher xG, so the win definitely feels deserved. And boy was it needed! The situation in the standings is still not great, but at least they are now four points behind the Champions League zone.

#1914. South American trips and rejected approaches: What Arne Slot has been doing since Liverpool exit

It’s now coming up to six months since Arne Slot was relieved of his duties as Liverpool head coach after two years in the role.

The Dutchman had the unenviable task of succeeding Jurgen Klopp in the Anfield dugout but delivered a surprise (and emphatic) Premier League title triumph in his first season in charge before the Reds’ fortunes nosedived dramatically last term.

The 48-year-old just about managed to achieve Champions League qualification in May, but the extent of the decline from 12 months previously made his position untenable, and he was dismissed to make way for Andoni Iraola.

In his latest Liverpool Confidential feature for the Daily Mail, Lewis Steele addressed the question of what Slot has been getting up to since his exit from Anfield, with the journalist ‘often asked’ about the Dutch tactician’s more recent endeavours.

He outlined that the former Reds boss has been ‘biding his time and enjoying holidays with loved ones’, including multiple trips to Ibiza and taking in football matches in Argentina and Brazil with his son Joep, along with attending games in his native Netherlands.

The 48-year-old turned down the chance to coach his country after the World Cup, as well as potentially ‘lucrative gig’ in Saudi Arabia. He also declined approaches from a few clubs in the summer, including AC Milan, who now have ex-Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim in charge.

Steele concluded that Slot is ‘waiting for the right opportunity’ to get back into the dugout and doesn’t believe that his ‘stock has fallen’ as much as some of his peers who’ve been sacked by other high-profile Premier League clubs.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The Dutchman’s Liverpool tenure may have ended on a low ebb, and the prevailing sentiment in May was that the time was right for a change, but it’d be wrong to describe his two-year spell at Anfield as a failure.

He vastly exceeded expectations by winning the Premier League at the first attempt, and while last season was undoubtedly a massive underachievement results-wise, it must be viewed in the context of Slot and the squad trying to navigate the horrendous grief of Diogo Jota’s tragic death.

That the 48-year-old has turned down job approaches in order to hold out for the ‘right opportunity’ indicates his confidence that he’ll get back on board the managerial carousel sooner rather than later, and that his reputation hasn’t been overly tarnished by the disappointment of 2025/26.

Most Liverpool fans would also acknowledge that Slot carried himself with tremendous dignity throughout his time with us, striking the perfect tone with his farewell message to supporters after his sacking and – most importantly – handling the loss of Jota with commendable grace.

It’s nice to hear that the Dutchman has been enjoying his time with family since departing Merseyside, and it wouldn’t surprise us in the slightest if he were to be back in the technical area with a new club over the next few months.

Wherever his career might take him from here, we wish him the best in his future endeavours.

#1913. Inter Milan vs Stuttgart - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 23 Nov 2026 15:39, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43

Separated by one point midway through the league phase, Inter Milan and Stuttgart will meet for a Champions League clash at San Siro on Wednesday evening.

After contrasting results last time out, Inter trail behind their German visitors, with both sides vying for entry to the knockout round playoffs.

Having exited at the first knockout stage last season - losing both playoff legs to Bodo/Glimt - Inter started this term's Champions League campaign slowly, taking nothing from their first two fixtures.

The Scudetto holders subsequently bounced back, though, posting consecutive wins without conceding a goal, against Shakhtar Donetsk and Feyenoord.

Shortly before the international break, Inter travelled to De Kuip and left with maximum points, thanks to goals from Yann Bisseck, Francesco Pio Esposito and Piotr Zielinski.

Such a start sums up their mixed fortunes since being humbled by Paris Saint-Germain in the 2025 final: Cristian Chivu's Champions League record as head coach reads seven wins and seven defeats.

Compared to life under his predecessor Simone Inzaghi, the Nerazzurri have been much less solid at the back, and they shipped yet more goals in a spectacular Serie A contest on Sunday night.

Despite Esposito's hat-trick, Inter ultimately had to settle for a 4-4 draw against local rivals Atalanta, and that left them three points behind surprise league leaders Lazio.

In stark contrast to their Italian counterparts, Stuttgart kicked off the league phase with back-to-back victories, scoring three goals against both Slovan Bratislava and Viking.

Then, they held Atletico Madrid to a 1-1 home draw, before visiting Istanbul to face Turkish champions Galatasaray on matchday four.

Already trailing by two goals inside 15 minutes, the German club never really recovered, suffering their first loss and slipping down to 14th place in the Champions League standings.

Despite holding on to highly-rated coach Sebastian Hoeness, Die Roten have struggled in the Bundesliga this season, losing half of their first 10 games.

While Inter were sharing eight goals in Bergamo, Stuttgart played out a 0-0 draw with Schalke last weekend, leaving them eighth in the table and eight points behind the top four.

Still, the Swabian side have recently improved a once porous defence, posting three clean sheets from four domestic matches before heading to Milan.

Although Inter threw away two points against Atalanta, they were able to welcome back their inspirational captain, as Lautaro Martinez made his return from injury with a late cameo.

Having conceded a stoppage-time penalty against his former club, Alessandro Bastoni will hope to fare better on Wednesday, when he returns from a Champions League suspension.

Benjamin Pavard made 88 appearances for Stuttgart between 2016 and 2019, and the Frenchman may join Bastoni in a three-man defence.

The hosts will be missing key midfielder and set-piece specialist Hakan Calhanoglu due to a thigh injury, while Ange Bonny is also ruled out.

Martinez must vie with Marcus Thuram and Manchester United target Esposito to feature up front, but there is no doubt about Stuttgart's star striker.

Ermedin Demirovic has already netted a club-record four goals in this season's Champions League campaign, added to five in the Bundesliga.

By contrast, Deniz Undav has yet to score in the German top flight, but he is still set to support Demirovic at San Siro.

Though Hoeness has most of his squad available, Luca Jaquez (rib), Leo Sauer (muscular) and Angelo Stiller (groin) are currently injured.

J. Martinez; Pavard, Akanji, Bastoni; Spence, Barella, Zielinski, Sucic, Dimarco; Esposito, L. Martinez

Bredlow; Hendriks, Chabot, Mittelstadt; Leweling, Karazor, Promel, Fuhrich; Undav, El Khannouss; Demirovic

It's either hit or miss for Inter, who have drawn none of their last 16 Champions League matches, and the Serie A champions will extend that trend with a home win.

Half of their goals in the league phase have arrived inside the final 15 minutes, so Stuttgart may be caught out in the closing stages.

#1912. Opposition insight for Milan-Frosinone: Form, injuries, predicted XI and more

AC Milan are looking to make it three consecutive wins tomorrow, but a high-flying newcomer in Frosinone could make that difficult.

Ruben Amorim and his men have an opportunity to really establish some momentum tomorrow evening, picking up where they left off before the break. However, it won’t be an easy game against Massimiliano Alvani’s Frosinone, who have impressed everyone so far.

Amorim even warned in his press conference that it will be a difficult one, especially since the Canarini have such a direct style.

➤ Manager: Massimiliano Alvini ➤ Form (all comps): W-D-W-W-L (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Serie A): Raimondo – 8 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Kvernadze, Schmid and Ghedjemis – 4 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

Frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

They are currently on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

It’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

So, what is behind this rise? As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

It doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

While collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly big-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

Moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

The Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

#1911. Lille vs Bayern Munich - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 16:10, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43

Stade Pierre-Mauroy will stage a gameweek five Champions League fixture between hosts Lille and six-time European winners Bayern Munich on Wednesday night.

The only previous two meetings between these teams came in the 2012-13 group stage when the German giants won both home and away by an aggregate score of 7-1 (1-0 away, 6-1 at home).

Lille are one of only three teams out of 36 in this season’s Champions League who enter the halfway stage of the League Phase without a single win to their name, drawing one and losing three of their first four matches, while they are one of 12 teams to have conceded at least 10 goals.

Les Dogues were beaten by Real Betis (3-2), Arsenal (3-0) and Galatasaray (4-2) before playing out a goalless stalemate with Bodo/Glimt in Norway on matchday four, leaving them sitting second-bottom in the 36-team standings and three points behind the playoff positions.

Head coach Davide Ancelotti – the son of five-time UCL winner and ex-Bayern boss Carlo Ancelotti – has seen his Lille side fare better in Ligue 1 this term, as they sit third in the table with 21 points after 11 matches (W6 D3 L2), five points adrift of leaders PSG.

However, Lille head into Wednesday’s contest on the back of a narrow 1-0 home defeat to fourth-placed Lyon last weekend. Les Dogues failed to score on the domestic front for the first time this season, with Ancelotti admitting that playing with a false nine ultimately led to a lack of presence in the penalty box.

Lille have been prolific on home soil in the Champions League, though, scoring in each of their last nine such matches, while they have also found the net in each of their last four UEFA encounters against German opposition.

Although Bayern Munich are one of only four teams yet to lose in this season’s Champions League, they currently sit down in 13th place in the League Phase standings after winning two and drawing two of their first four fixtures.

A thumping 5-0 victory over Bodo/Glimt on matchday one was followed by two action-packed draws with Viking FK (3-3) and Arsenal (2-2), conceding late goals in both games. However, the Bavarian giants returned to winning ways with a 2-0 away success over Atletico Madrid three weeks ago.

Supporters have certainly not been short of entertainment when watching Bayern, as they have now scored at least twice in 12 of their last 13 Champions League games, while their last 10 matches in the competition have produced a whopping 50 goals.

After missing five games following a recent health scare, head coach Vincent Kompany made a welcome return to the touchline with his left arm in a sling for Bayern’s Bundesliga clash at home to Koln last Friday. However, his side were held to a frustrating 1-1 draw, surrendering top spot to Borussia Dortmund who now sit two points clear.

Bayern will be keen to make a swift return to winning ways as they endeavour to climb back into the top-eight of the UCL League Phase, and they should be confident of success on Wednesday having won seven of their last 10 European away matches against French opposition.

Lille are still having to cope without Tiago Santos and Hamza Igamane who are recovering from long-term knee injuries, but Ethan Mbappe is available to return from a three-match UCL suspension and is set to rival Dilane Bakwa for a start on the right flank.

After returning to training and then featuring as a substitute against Lyon, Ayase Ueda may be in contention to start up front after recovering from a foot injury, while 40-year-old Olivier Giroud is also a natural centre-forward option at Ancelotti’s disposal.

Tanguy Nianzou, who made four UCL appearances for Bayern in the 2021-22 campaign, is likely to start at the heart of the defence alongside Alexsandro, while Nabil Bentaleb, Ngal'ayel Mukau and Benjamin Andre are all set to play in midfield.

As for Bayern, they suffered a major injury blow last Friday as 2026 Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane suffered a torn syndesmosis ligament which required surgery. The striker is now expected to be sidelined for at least a few months.

Manuel Neuer (foot), Alphonso Davies (knee/muscle), Serge Gnabry (hamstring) and Ismael Saibari (ankle) are also in the treatment room, while Luis Diaz (hamstring) and Michael Olise (foot) are both doubtful, the latter of whom was seen on crutches and wearing a protective boot after the draw with Koln.

In the absence of Kane, the likes of Diaz - if fit - Jamal Musiala, Noah Codjo-Evora, 17, and Bastian Assomo, 16, are potential candidates to lead the line for Bayern.

Lennart Karl is another attacking option at Kompany’s disposal. At the age of 18 years and 276 days, he has scored five UCL goals, the fourth-most by any player before turning 19. A goal on Wednesday would see him equal Raul in third place, behind Lamine Yamal (11) and Kylian Mbappe (10).

Lille can feel quietly optimistic about claiming a positive result on home soil against a weakened Bayern side dealing with a mounting injury crisis, particularly with the absence of talisman Kane representing a major blow to the visitors' frontline.

However, even if Kompany is forced to field a makeshift attack, the Bavarian giants still possess enough overall quality and have our backing to edge a closely-fought contest.
